CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

What this is

ConR is an R package (GPL-2, roxygen2 7.2.3, no CRAN release since the rgdal/rgeos retirement) that computes the population metrics behind IUCN Red List criteria A–D and assigns threat categories, designed to run over hundreds/thousands of taxa at once. Spatial work is done with sf/terra (the old sp/rgdal stack is gone).

Development workflow

Any development that is not truly minimal must happen on a dedicated branch, never directly on master. Branch from the current master (or devel), keep one branch per concern, and open a PR to merge back — this is how the existing history works (devel, new_func, paral_test, proj_eoo_test all merged via PRs). “Truly minimal” means a typo, a one-line doc tweak, or a comment; anything that touches function behaviour, signatures, DESCRIPTION/NAMESPACE, or adds files gets a branch.

git switch -c fix-<short-topic> master

Regenerate NAMESPACE and man/ with devtools::document() in the same commit as the roxygen change, and run devtools::test() before opening the PR.

Commands

Run from the package root with Rscript -e "..." (devtools/roxygen2/testthat are not in Suggests; install them if missing).

devtools::load_all(".")                      # load without installing (main dev loop)
devtools::document()                         # regenerate NAMESPACE + man/*.Rd from roxygen
devtools::test()                             # run all tests
devtools::test(filter = "5")                 # run only tests/testthat/test-5.R
testthat::test_file("tests/testthat/test-3.R")
devtools::check()                            # full R CMD check
R CMD INSTALL .
pkgdown::build_site()                        # -> docs/ (deployed by .github/workflows/pkgdown.yaml on push to master)

There is no tests/testthat.R driver, so R CMD check does not run the test suite — use devtools::test() explicitly.

Tests are numbered, not named after the function they cover: test-1 EOO.computing, test-2 subpop.comp, test-3 criterion_B, test-4 locations.comp, test-5 pop.decline.fit, test-6 pop.decline, test-7 criterion_A, test-8 criterion_C, test-9 pop.decline.test. Several use context() (deprecated in testthat 3e); the package is not on testthat edition 3.

git may fail here with “detected dubious ownership” — fix once with git config --global --add safe.directory D:/MonDossierR/ConR_orig.

Architecture

Two layers, deliberately separated:

  1. Metric functions compute biological/geographic indicators from raw data: EOO.computing, AOO.computing, locations.comp, subpop.comp, severe_frag, AOH.estimation, AOO.decline, pop.decline (+ pop.decline.fit, .test), pop.fluctuation, EOO.sensitivity.
  2. criterion_* functions (criterion_A/B/C/D) orchestrate: they either accept pre-computed metrics or call the metric functions themselves, then delegate the threshold logic to the pure cat_criterion_* functions (cat_criterion_a/b/c), which take numeric vectors + threshold vectors and return category vectors.

Keep that split when adding features: thresholds and IUCN category logic belong in cat_criterion_*; spatial/statistical computation belongs in the metric functions.

Multi-criteria consolidation happens outside the criterion functions, in the order used by vignettes/articles/ConR.Rmd: merge the criterion_* data frames by tax → near.threatened() per sub-criterion to split LC from NT → cat_mult_criteria() for the consensus category and the main/auxiliary criteria. cat_downlist() downgrades categories (e.g. regional assessments).

Conventions that cut across the codebase

  • Occurrence input XY/x: a data.frame whose positions matter and names do not — col 1 latitude (numeric, decimal degrees), col 2 longitude, col 3 taxon name. Functions rename them to ddlat, ddlon, tax internally.

  • coord.check() is the mandatory front door for any occurrence-based function. It coerces/validates coordinates, sanitizes taxon names, optionally projects, splits by taxon, and returns list(list_data, issue_close_to_anti, issue_long_span, issue_nrow, unique_occs). The issue_* slots feed the warning columns of the final results.

  • Projections go through proj_crs(), never raw st_crs() strings. proj_type = "cea" (ESRI:54034, the default) plus shortcuts "Antarctic", "Africa_eac"; anything else is an EPSG code or string passed through. EOO additionally has mode = "spheroid" (default, geodetic) vs "planar" (projects first).

  • Parallelism is the same three-line idiom everywhere — copy it rather than inventing a new one:

    cl <- activate_parallel(parallel, NbeCores)   # PSOCK + doSNOW
`%d%` <- c_par(parallel)                      # %dopar% or %do%
pro_res <- display_progress_bar(show_progress, max_pb = length(list_data))
# foreach(..., .options.snow = pro_res$opts) %d% { ... }
if (parallel) parallel::stopCluster(cl)

    Every user-facing loop takes parallel, NbeCores, show_progress.

  • Optional dependencies are Suggests, guarded at the top of the function with requireNamespace(..., quietly = TRUE) + stop("The 'x' package is required..."). lwgeom gates EOO.computing()/criterion_B(); alphahull gates alpha-hull ranges. Tests are written to expect that error and skip() when the package is absent.

  • Non-standard-evaluation symbols used inside foreach/data.table must be declared in R/globals.R.

  • Removed functionality is kept as a .Defunct() stub (IUCN.eval, map.res) rather than deleted.

Files worth knowing

  • R/cell.occupied.R — grid-overlay engine shared by AOO and locations; repeated random grid translations keep the minimum number of occupied cells (nbe_rep).
  • R/locations.comp.R — two methods: "fixed_grid" (cell_size_locations, km) and "sliding_scale" (rel_cell_size × max pairwise distance, Rivers et al. 2010); also handles threat polygons via threat_list/threat_weight.
  • R/pop.decline.fit.R + R/ICtab.mod.select.R — nls.multstart/segmented model fitting (linear, quadratic, exponential, logistic, general_logistic, piecewise) and IC-based model selection feeding criteria A and C.
  • R/EOO.sensitivity.R also defines over.valid.poly(); R/over.valid.poly.R is empty.

man/*.Rd and NAMESPACE are generated — edit the roxygen blocks and run devtools::document(). data/ holds the example datasets documented in R/dataset.ex.R (dataset.ex, example_criterionA/C, example_tutorial, land, Madagascar.protec, Malagasy.amphibian); data-raw/ is gitignored. dummy_dist() generates throwaway multi-species occurrence data for tests and examples.

The long-form tutorial is vignettes/articles/ConR.Rmd (built PDF alongside it) — it is the reference for the intended end-to-end workflow.
